title: Nullable Value Types and Nullability
learningObjectives: Explain the purpose and behavior of nullable value types and nullability in C#.
Choose an appropriate type for a simple application scenario.
Read and explain original C# code that demonstrates the lesson concepts.
Predict deterministic program output and identify common mistakes.
Compile and execute a small .NET 10 console example to verify the result.

understand.concept: A nullable value type such as int? can represent either a value of its underlying type or null. Nullable reference annotations such as string? communicate that a reference may be null. These are related nullability concepts but use different type-system mechanisms.
understand.whyItMatters: Real applications often have optional or not-yet-known data. Explicit null handling makes that state visible and reduces runtime null-reference errors.
understand.analogy: A nullable value is like a form field that may contain a number or be left unanswered.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not mean null is a numeric value. Nullable value types wrap an underlying value type, while nullable reference annotations primarily express compiler-checked intent.

explain.narrative:
## Nullable value types

Append ? to a non-nullable value type, such as int?, to allow either a value or null. Use HasValue, Value or GetValueOrDefault to inspect it, but avoid accessing Value when HasValue is false.

## Null-coalescing

The ?? operator supplies a fallback when a nullable value or reference is null. The ??= operator assigns a fallback only when the left operand is null.

## Nullable reference types

With nullable reference types enabled, string means a non-null reference by default and string? means null is permitted. This feature adds compiler analysis and warnings; it does not create a distinct runtime string type or automatically prevent null at runtime.

## Null-conditional access

The ?. operator stops member access when the receiver is null and produces a nullable result. Use it when the absence of an object is a normal possibility.

## Baseline

Examples target .NET 10 and C# 14 with nullable analysis enabled.

examples.title: Declare a nullable integer
examples.explanation: int? can contain either an int value or null. HasValue reports whether an underlying value is present.

examples.title: Provide a fallback with ??
examples.explanation: The null-coalescing operator uses the fallback value when selectedSeats is null.

examples.title: Use GetValueOrDefault
examples.explanation: GetValueOrDefault returns the underlying value or the default value of the underlying type when null.

examples.title: Use nullable reference annotation
examples.explanation: string? documents that the reference may be null. The ?? operator supplies a non-null fallback.

examples.title: Use null-conditional access
examples.explanation: The ?. operator skips member access when message is null and produces a nullable result.
